why: Reduce competition between fine regional ground detail and placed plants/residents while retaining distinct regional earth palettes and the existing artwork.
change: Regional ground receives a stronger earth-colored base wash: muted olive-gold for Cerrado and dusty tan for Caatinga. It is applied before habitats/soil and before roads or world sprites. The original Mata Atlantica treatment remains the same.
checks: Twelve explicit DOM/OffscreenCanvas isolated atlas pixel cases pass; baseline uses its own old tint so contamination reproduction is independent of the intentional color change.
Six actual-art main/worker pixel comparisons and terrain cancellation/reuse/fallback/error cases pass.
Both Mata Atlantica road/no-road fixture hashes equal the prior atlas-isolation evidence.
Normal player selection of all three biomes, regional planting, native playtest climate and editor return pass without browser errors.
JavaScript syntax and diff whitespace checks pass.
Individual natural-object browser journey also passes on the new terrain: selection, exact history, invalid edits, drag/cancel, reload, native playtest and return.
visualFindings: Placed plants, residents and buildings separate more clearly from the quieter regional ground in the inspected complete scenes.
Cerrado remains olive/gold with red-earth roads; Caatinga retains its warm tan ground and ochre roads.
Inspected night scenes retain consistent ambient tint and contact; inspected rain boards preserve the main silhouettes.
Fine painted ground is still present. This is a contrast correction, not approval of all regional landscape artwork.
Selected Macambira ring, above-sprite label and inspector remain legible on the revised Caatinga ground.
limits: Only the listed four normal-scale nature boards and five full scenes were visually inspected for this change. Uninspected boards in capture reports are not visual acceptance.
All-catalog close/overview weather, mixed habitats and neighboring contexts still need the corresponding full review.
No sprite assets, proportions, texture repeat scale, simulation rules or native definitions changed.
Broader resident motion, performance, memory, recovery and player-experience release gates remain open.
